name: Pwyll

attributes.attribute: Prince of Dyfed and hero of the Mabinogion
exchanged places with Arawn and defeated Hafgan
husband of Rhiannon and father of Pryderi

sources: Gantz, Jeffrey, trans. *The Mabinogion*. (New York: Barnes & Noble Books, 1976).
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Pwyll, Prince of Dyfed, is a Welsh hero. He is one of the primary heroes of the Mabinogion. In the first branch he exchanges places with the Otherworldly king Arawn. Arawn was hounded by his enemy Hafgan. Hoping Pwyll could save his country, Arawn asked him to take his place. Pwyll agreed and ruled well in the Otherworld. He refused to sleep with Arawn's queen. At the end of the year he met Hafgan in single combat and defeated him. Back in his own world Pwyll fell for Rhiannon, who appeared on a white horse. When he called to her, she stopped, and they married. After the birth of their son Pryderi, Rhiannon was accused of harm, for the child was missing. Pwyll punished her to serve as a horse until Pryderi returned. Their reign then prospered.

okr.objective: Describe Pwyll as a primary hero of the Welsh Mabinogion.
key_results: Names Pwyll as Prince of Dyfed and a Mabinogion hero
Records his exchange with Arawn and his defeat of Hafgan
Tells his courtship of Rhiannon and the return of Pryderi
